::: {.callout style="border-left: 6px solid #D99B8F; --bs-callout-border: #D99B8F; padding: 1.5rem; border-radius: 8px; margin-bottom: 1rem;"}
Individual shorebirds vary a lot in how they use their sites in the estuary, so we want to quantify how much birds of the same species differ in this site use, and whether it might varies with tide.

There are two questions:

1.   **Do birds of the same species use sites differently?**

2.  **If so, do they use different sites (private sites), or the same sites in different proportions (unequal use of shared sites)?**

A few metrics will help us answering these questions, and below is a conceptual diagram in which metric to employ depending the question. *Most of the analysis is derivative of the work of Balsega ([2009](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.1466-8238.2009.00490.x), [2012](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.1466-8238.2011.00756.x) & [2013](https://besjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/2041-210X.12029)))*
:::

![](/material/site_use_metric.png){fig-align="center" width="100%"}

::: blockquote-blue
*visit_hours_tide* is then used onward so, the same rule applies in the data-set: **\< 1 hour gap between two runs are considered as a unique use of the area covered by a Motus station - the bird remained in the area within this hour gap**.

# Setup data

```{r data, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE, eval=TRUE, results='asis' , fig.align='center' }
# Ensure correct format for analysis
visit_hours_tide <- visit_hours_tide %>%
  mutate(Band.ID      = as.character(Band.ID),
         tideCategory = factor(tideCategory,
                               levels = c("Diurnal_High", "Diurnal_Low",
                                          "Nocturnal_High", "Nocturnal_Low")))%>%
  filter(!is.na(Band.ID), !is.na(recvDeployName)) 

# Carry sample size
n_tags_species <- visit_hours_tide %>%
  filter(!is.na(Band.ID)) %>%
  distinct(speciesEN, Band.ID) %>%
  count(speciesEN, name = "n_indiv")

n_tags_species %>%
  DT::datatable()

```

# Time budget per site

We use `overlap_h`: the duration (hours) each bird was *confirmed present* at each site in each hourly tide-bin. Summing `overlap_h` per bird x site gives a duration-based "time budget" to assess the question **"how much does this bird rely on this site"**.

```{r site-use-table, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE, eval=TRUE, results='asis' , fig.align='center' }
# Time budget (%) all
site_use_ind <- visit_hours_tide %>%
  
  group_by(speciesEN, Band.ID, recvDeployName) %>%
  
  summarise(effort_h = sum(overlap_h, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(speciesEN, Band.ID) %>%
  mutate(p = 100 * effort_h / sum(effort_h)) %>%                            # p = %
  ungroup()

# Time budget (%) tideCategory
site_use_ind_tide <- visit_hours_tide %>%
  
  group_by(speciesEN, Band.ID, tideCategory, recvDeployName) %>%
  
  summarise(effort_h = sum(overlap_h, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(speciesEN, Band.ID, tideCategory) %>%
  mutate(p = 100 * effort_h / sum(effort_h)) %>%                            # p = %
  ungroup()

# Plot
ggplot(site_use_ind_tide,
       aes(x = fct_reorder(Band.ID, p, .fun = max), y = p, fill = recvDeployName)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8) +
  facet_grid(tideCategory ~ speciesEN, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(0, 50, 100), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(
    title    = "Individual site-use composition",
    subtitle = "% of tracked time (overlap_h) each bird spent per site",
    x        = "Individual (Band.ID)", y = "% of time budget", fill = "Site") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x        = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5, size = 7),
    legend.position    = "bottom",
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
    strip.text.x       = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 0, vjust = 0.5),
    strip.text.y       = element_text(angle = 0),
    panel.border       = element_rect(colour = "grey30", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.7),
    panel.spacing.x    = unit(0.8, "lines"),
    panel.spacing.y    = unit(0.4, "lines"))
```

![](/material/map_colour_site.png){fig-align="center" width="100%"}

Here, we can already see that for some species, most of individuals use sites in a different manner within the estuary, and for other species, most individuals use site in a similar manner.

However, we need to build some metrics capable to inform the degree of this dissimilarity (or similarity) within site use between individuals of a same species.

And going deeper, we ask whether birds **(1) use their sites differently, and if they do (2) whether they use different sites, or the same sites but dis similarly.**

# Metrics

## Definition

We need to first manually build function to compute **Jensen-Shannon Divergence** metric (JSD), and store results in a matrix. Then we can use `betapart` package ([Balsega et Orme - 2012](https://besjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/j.2041-210X.2012.00224.x)) to extract Jaccard and Bray-Curtis metrics.

![](/material/jsd_definition.png){fig-align="center" width="100%"}

```{r divergence-functions, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE, eval=TRUE, results='asis' , fig.align='center' }

# Jensen-Shannon Divergence (JSD) function definition
calculate_jsd <- function(p, q) {
  eps <- 1e-10
  p <- (p + eps) / sum(p + eps)
  q <- (q + eps) / sum(q + eps)
  m <- (p + q) / 2
  0.5 * sum(p * log2(p / m)) + 0.5 * sum(q * log2(q / m))
}

# Pairwise divergence individuals (rows, named by Band.ID) x sites (cols), rows sum to 100
compute_divergence <- function(prop_mat) {

  if (nrow(prop_mat) < 2) return(NULL)   # need at least 2 birds to compare

  pa_mat <- (prop_mat > 0) * 1           # presence/absence version, for Jaccard

  # Use Balsega's (2013) package
  jac  <- betapart::beta.pair(as.data.frame(pa_mat),  index.family = "jaccard")     # Incidence-based pair-wise dissimilarities
  bray <- betapart::beta.pair.abund(as.data.frame(prop_mat), index.family = "bray") # Abundance-based pair-wise dissimilarities

  ids <- rownames(prop_mat)         
  pr  <- combn(nrow(prop_mat), 2)   # same pair order as a `dist` object's internal storage

  jsd_vals <- apply(pr, 2, function(ix) calculate_jsd(prop_mat[ix[1], ], prop_mat[ix[2], ]))

  tibble(
    Band.ID_1     = ids[pr[1, ]],
    Band.ID_2     = ids[pr[2, ]],
    JSD           = round(jsd_vals, 3),                          # "overall dissimilarity"
    jac_total     = round(as.numeric(jac$beta.jac),       3),
    jac_turnover  = round(as.numeric(jac$beta.jtu),        3),   # "different sites used"
    jac_nested    = round(as.numeric(jac$beta.jne),        3),   # "subset of sites"
    bray_total    = round(as.numeric(bray$beta.bray),      3),
    bray_balanced = round(as.numeric(bray$beta.bray.bal),  3),   # "uneven use of shared sites"
    bray_gradient = round(as.numeric(bray$beta.bray.gra),  3))
}

# Helper: long-format individual x site proportion matrix -> wide matrix
to_prop_matrix <- function(df) {
  wide <- df %>%
    select(Band.ID, recvDeployName, p) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = recvDeployName, values_from = p, values_fill = 0)
  m <- as.matrix(wide[, -1])
  rownames(m) <- wide$Band.ID
  m
}

# Results
divergence_global <- site_use_ind %>%
  group_by(speciesEN) %>%
  group_split() %>%
  map(function(df) {
    mat <- to_prop_matrix(df)
    res <- compute_divergence(mat)
    if (!is.null(res)) res$speciesEN <- df$speciesEN[1]
    res
  }) %>%
  compact() %>%
  bind_rows()
```

## Jensen Shannon Divergence: overall dissimilarity

```{r JSD, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE, eval=TRUE, results='asis' , fig.align='center'}

jsd_sum <- divergence_global %>%
  group_by(speciesEN) %>%
  summarise(med = median(JSD),
            sd  = sd(JSD),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(n_tags_species, by = "speciesEN") %>%
  mutate(lo    = pmax(med - sd, 0),          # keep bars inside 0-1
         hi    = pmin(med + sd, 1),
         label = fct_reorder(paste0(speciesEN, "  (n = ", n_indiv, ")"), med))

ggplot(jsd_sum, aes(y = label)) +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi, colour = med),
                 orientation = "y", linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(aes(x = med, colour = med), size = 4) +
  scale_colour_gradient(low = "#2ECC71", high = "#F28E16",
                        limits = c(0, 1), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.03))) +
  labs(x = "Jensen-Shannon divergence (median ± SD)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y        = element_text(face = "italic"))

```

::: {.callout collapse="true" title="See population summary plot" appearance="simple"}

```{r JSD-table-indiv, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE, eval=TRUE, results='asis' , fig.align='center'}
library(gt)
jsd_sum <- divergence_global %>%
  group_by(speciesEN) %>%
  summarise(med     = median(JSD),
            sd      = sd(JSD),

            .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(n_tags_species, by = "speciesEN") %>%

             lo        = "Lower",
             hi        = "Upper")
```
:::

## Jaccard & Bray-Curtis: dissimilarity decomposition

How much of their overall dissimilarity comes from **not sharing sites** (Jaccard turnover) versus **sharing sites but using them unevenly** (Bray-Curtis balanced variation)?

```{r plot-decomposition, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE, eval=TRUE, results='asis' , fig.align='center'}
species_lab <- divergence_global %>%
  group_by(speciesEN) %>%
  summarise(med_jsd = median(JSD),
            n_pairs = n(),
            n_indiv = n_distinct(c(Band.ID_1, Band.ID_2)),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(label = fct_reorder(
           paste0(speciesEN, "\n n = ", n_indiv, "\n pairs = ", n_pairs),
           med_jsd, .desc = TRUE)) %>%
  select(speciesEN, label)

decomp_long <- divergence_global %>%
  select(speciesEN, JSD, jac_turnover, bray_balanced) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(JSD, jac_turnover, bray_balanced),
               names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") %>%
  left_join(species_lab, by = "speciesEN") %>%
  mutate(metric = dplyr::recode(metric,
    JSD           = "Overall dissimilarity (JSD)",
    jac_turnover  = "Different sites used (Jaccard)",
    bray_balanced = "Uneven use of shared sites (Bray-Curtis)"),
    metric = factor(metric, levels = c(
      "Overall dissimilarity (JSD)",
      "Different sites used (Jaccard)",
      "Uneven use of shared sites (Bray-Curtis)")))

plot_decomposition <- decomp_long %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = label, y = value, fill = metric)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.75, outlier.shape = 16, outlier.size = 1,
               position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "Overall dissimilarity (JSD)"                = "grey40",
    "Different sites used (Jaccard)"             = "#D95F02",
    "Uneven use of shared sites (Bray-Curtis)"   = "#1B9E77")) +
  labs(
    title    = "Dissimilarity decomposition: private sites, or uneven use of shared sites?",
    subtitle = "Within-species pairwise comparisons",
    x = NULL, y = "Dissimilarity (0-1)", fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x        = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 9),
    legend.position    = "top",
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())

plot_decomposition
```

::: {.callout collapse="true" title="See table data" appearance="simple"}
```{r plot-decomposition-table, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE, eval=TRUE, results='asis' , fig.align='center' }
library(DT)
# Summary per species x metric (the values behind the boxes)
n_species <- divergence_global %>%
  group_by(speciesEN) %>%
  summarise(n_indiv = n_distinct(c(Band.ID_1, Band.ID_2)), .groups = "drop")

decomp_long %>%
  group_by(speciesEN, metric) %>%
  summarise(n_pairs = n(),
            median  = median(value),
            sd      = sd(value),
            q1      = quantile(value, 0.25),
            q3      = quantile(value, 0.75),
            min     = min(value),
            max     = max(value),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(n_species, by = "speciesEN") %>%
  relocate(n_indiv, .after = metric)

# Pair-level values (what each box is built from)
divergence_global %>%
  dplyr::select(speciesEN, Band.ID_1, Band.ID_2,
                JSD, jac_turnover, bray_balanced) %>%
  DT::datatable()

```
:::

A species where Jaccar turnover value (orange box) sits above the Bray-Curtis balanced variation (green box) highlights that individuals are mostly diverging in site use because **they use different (private) sites**. Inversely, individuals **use same (shared/common) sites, use them very much differently (unequal use)**.

## Tide and diel periods

We are now interested about the same question but depending the tide and diel. `divergence_tide` is the tide-specific version of `divergence_global` implementing the same pairwise metrics, but computed separately inside each tide category.

Birds are only compared if they were detected in the same tide category. A bird with no data in Nocturnal_Low is not in that tide’s pairs. Groups with fewer than 2 birds are skipped.

```{r divergence-tide, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE, eval=TRUE}
divergence_tide <- site_use_ind_tide %>%
  group_by(speciesEN, tideCategory) %>%
  group_split() %>%
  map(function(df) {
    mat <- to_prop_matrix(df)
    res <- compute_divergence(mat)
    if (!is.null(res)) {
      res$speciesEN    <- df$speciesEN[1]
      res$tideCategory <- df$tideCategory[1]
    }
    res
  }) %>%
  compact() %>%
  bind_rows()
```

```{r pairwise-tide, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE, eval=TRUE, results='asis' , fig.align='center', fig.height=9.5, fig.width= 8}

  summarise(med_jsd = median(JSD), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(med_jsd)) %>%

# labels with n and pairs, computed per species x tide
species_lab_tide <- divergence_tide %>%

            .groups = "drop") %>%

         sp_order  = match(speciesEN, species_order)) %>%

  mutate(label = factor(label_chr, levels = unique(label_chr))) %>%
  select(speciesEN, tideCategory, label)

decomp_long_tide <- divergence_tide %>%
  select(speciesEN, tideCategory, JSD, jac_turnover, bray_balanced) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(JSD, jac_turnover, bray_balanced),
               names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") %>%
  left_join(species_lab_tide, by = c("speciesEN", "tideCategory")) %>%
  mutate(metric = dplyr::recode(metric,
    JSD           = "Overall dissimilarity (JSD)",
    jac_turnover  = "Different sites used (Jaccard)",
    bray_balanced = "Uneven use of shared sites (Bray-Curtis)"),
    metric = factor(metric, levels = c(
      "Overall dissimilarity (JSD)",
      "Different sites used (Jaccard)",
      "Uneven use of shared sites (Bray-Curtis)")))

plot_decomposition_tide <- decomp_long_tide %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = label, y = value, fill = metric)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.75, outlier.shape = 16, outlier.size = 1,

  facet_wrap(~ tideCategory, ncol = 1, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "Overall dissimilarity (JSD)"                = "grey40",
    "Different sites used (Jaccard)"             = "#D95F02",
    "Uneven use of shared sites (Bray-Curtis)"   = "#1B9E77")) +
  labs(
    title    = "Dissimilarity decomposition: private sites, or uneven use of shared sites?",
    subtitle = "Within-species pairwise comparisons, by tide category",
    x = NULL, y = "Dissimilarity (0-1)", fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +

plot_decomposition_tide
```

# Statistical individual differences

## Definition

**PERMANOVA** (`vegan::adonis2`, Anderson 2001) tests whether groups (here: individual birds) differ in the *location* (centroid) of their site-use composition, using a permutation test on the distance matrix itself rather than treating pairwise distances as independent samples (as would do Kruskal or ANOVA). Permutation test is distribution-free, robust to non-normal/compositional data, and is standard in ecology for kind of question.

For each species we use the four `tideCategory` per bird as replicate observations and test `Bray-Curtis distance ~ Band.ID`.

We pair this with **PERMDISP** (`vegan::betadisper` + `permutest`, [Anderson 2006](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1541-0420.2005.00440.x); [Anderson & Walsh 2013](https://doi.org/10.1890/12-2010.1)) which tests whether individuals differ in *dispersion* (within-bird consistency) rather than in mean composition. This matters because PERMANOVA can be significant either because individuals truly use different site compositions, **or** because some individuals are simply more variable than others, and PERMDISP tells which one.

```{r permanova-function, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE, eval=TRUE, results='asis' , fig.align='center' }
run_species_permanova <- function(sp_df, min_indiv = 3) {

  n_indiv <- n_distinct(sp_df$Band.ID)

  if (n_indiv < min_indiv) {
    return(tibble(n_indiv = n_indiv, n_obs = nrow(sp_df),
                  F = NA, R2 = NA, p_permanova = NA,
                  F_disp = NA, p_dispersion = NA,
                  note = paste0("Skipped: only ", n_indiv, " tagged individuals (need >= ", min_indiv, ")")))
  }

  # Build one row per Band.ID x tideCategory replicate profile (up to 4 rows per bird), site proportions in the columns:
  wide <- sp_df %>%
    mutate(row_id = paste(Band.ID, tideCategory, sep = "__")) %>%
    select(row_id, Band.ID, recvDeployName, p) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = recvDeployName, values_from = p, values_fill = 0)

  meta <- wide %>% select(row_id, Band.ID)
  mat  <- as.matrix(wide %>% select(-row_id, -Band.ID))
  rownames(mat) <- wide$row_id

  keep <- rowSums(mat) > 0     # drop empty replicate rows
  mat  <- mat[keep, , drop = FALSE]
  meta <- meta[keep, ]

  if (nrow(mat) < (n_indiv + 1)) {
    return(tibble(n_indiv = n_indiv, n_obs = nrow(mat),
                  F = NA, R2 = NA, p_permanova = NA,
                  F_disp = NA, p_dispersion = NA,
                  note = "Skipped: not enough replicate profiles per individual"))
  }

  d <- vegan::vegdist(mat, method = "bray")

  perm <- tryCatch(
    vegan::adonis2(d ~ Band.ID, data = meta, permutations = 999),
    error = function(e) NULL)

  disp <- tryCatch({
    bd <- vegan::betadisper(d, meta$Band.ID)
    vegan::permutest(bd, permutations = 999)
  }, error = function(e) NULL)

  tibble(
    n_indiv      = n_indiv,
    n_obs        = nrow(mat),
    F            = if (!is.null(perm)) round(perm$F[1], 2) else NA,
    R2           = if (!is.null(perm)) round(perm$R2[1], 3) else NA,
    p_permanova  = if (!is.null(perm)) perm$`Pr(>F)`[1] else NA,
    F_disp       = if (!is.null(disp)) round(disp$tab$F[1], 2) else NA,
    p_dispersion = if (!is.null(disp)) disp$tab$`Pr(>F)`[1] else NA,
    note         = "")
}
```

## Results

```{r permanova-run, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE, eval=TRUE, results='asis' , fig.align='center' }
permanova_results <- site_use_ind_tide %>%
  group_by(speciesEN) %>%
  group_split() %>%
  map_dfr(~ run_species_permanova(.x) %>% mutate(speciesEN = .x$speciesEN[1], .before = 1)) %>%
  mutate(
    sig_permanova = case_when(
      is.na(p_permanova)      ~ "",
      p_permanova   < 0.001   ~ "***",
      p_permanova   < 0.01    ~ "**",
      p_permanova   < 0.05    ~ "*",
      TRUE                    ~ "ns"),
    interpretation = case_when(
      is.na(p_permanova)                                ~ note,
      p_permanova < 0.05 & (is.na(p_dispersion) | p_dispersion >= 0.05) ~
        "Individuals differ significantly in mean site-use composition (robust)",
      p_permanova < 0.05 & p_dispersion < 0.05           ~
        "Significant, but dispersion also differs - interpret with caution (Anderson & Walsh 2013)",
      TRUE ~ "No significant individual-level difference detected"))

permanova_results %>%
  arrange(p_permanova) %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(title = md("**Table.** PERMANOVA test of individual site-use divergence, per species")) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(F, R2, F_disp), decimals = 2) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(p_permanova, p_dispersion), decimals = 3) %>%
  cols_label(
    speciesEN      = "Species",
    n_indiv        = "N indiv.",
    n_obs          = "N profiles",
    F              = "F",
    R2             = "R\u00b2",
    p_permanova    = "p (PERMANOVA)",
    sig_permanova  = "",
    F_disp         = "F (disp.)",
    p_dispersion   = "p (PERMDISP)",
    interpretation = "Interpretation") %>%
  tab_footnote(footnote = md(
    "**PERMANOVA** (`vegan::adonis2`, Bray-Curtis, 999 permutations) tests whether Band.ID explains site-use composition. **PERMDISP** (`betadisper`) tests whether individuals differ in *within-bird* consistency rather than in mean composition - a significant PERMANOVA alongside a significant PERMDISP should be interpreted cautiously (Anderson & Walsh 2013)."))
```
